settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: A public constructor/flag allowStoredEntriesWithDataDescriptor exists specifically to opt into/vary this behavior, and ZipArchiveInputStream documents that ZipFile is preferred for file-based reading.
The library intentionally exposes compressed/uncompressed byte statistics (COMPRESS-445, changes.xml) so callers can detect zip bombs; the responsibility for limits may be considered the caller's.
readStoredEntry/readStored were not fully read line-by-line here, so any internal size validation inside readStoredEntry is unconfirmed.
The parsing code also verifies CRC and sizes in several paths (counter to a naive OOM claim), though the buffering still occurs before validation of consumed data.
candidates.description: In ZipArchiveInputStream.readStored, when the current entry is STORED and uses a data descriptor, the code calls readStoredEntry() and only then serves data from lastStoredEntry (a ByteArrayInputStream). readStoredEntry() reads the whole entry into an in-memory buffer before returning, so the size of the allocation is controlled by the attacker-supplied archive (the entry's uncompressed/compressed size, i.e., the amount of stored data preceding the descriptor), not by the caller's read() length. An archive containing a large STORED entry with the data-descriptor bit set causes the entire entry to be buffered in memory regardless of how little the caller consumes, which can exhaust the heap on a constrained consumer. readStoredEntry() is also reachable from ZipFile.getInputStream for data-descriptor stored entries (per the ZipFile source searched), so both the streaming and seekable APIs can trigger a full-entry buffering step. This is a resource-consumption concern rather than memory corruption; the library provides getCompressedCount()/getUncompressedCount() statistics for callers to implement their own limits, but no built-in cap is applied here.
missing_evidence: The full body of readStoredEntry() (allocation logic and any size checks) was not read in this snapshot.
Whether the STORED+descriptor path is only entered when allowStoredEntriesWithDataDescriptor is true was not fully traced.
No measurement of the actual memory ceiling or confirmation that crafted input reaches this path at runtime was performed.
ZipFile.getInputStream's exact reachability to readStoredEntry was only inferred from a search excerpt, not read in full.
preconditions: Caller uses ZipArchiveInputStream (or ZipFile.getInputStream) to process an untrusted ZIP archive.
Archive contains a STORED entry whose general-purpose bit 3 (data descriptor) is set.
No external size/entry limit or memory budget is enforced by the caller.
allowStoredEntriesWithDataDescriptor is enabled where required for streaming reads (ZipArchiveInputStream constructor with that flag), which is needed for the STORED+descriptor path.
candidates.title: ZipArchiveInputStream STORED-with-data-descriptor entries are fully buffered into a ByteArrayInputStream (unbounded memory, potential OOM/DoS)

counter_evidence: The code comment explicitly claims diff is bounded by a single buffered read and 'can't exceed the range of int', suggesting the invariant is intended to hold.
getBytesInflated() deliberately reconciles Inflater counters for Java < 7 wrap behavior (TWO_EXP_32 loop), reducing the chance of a large spurious difference.
diff > 0 is required before pushback is invoked, which guards the negative path in normal cases.
candidates.description: In closeEntry(), after draining/skipping, the code computes 'final int diff = (int) (current.bytesReadFromStream - inB);' where bytesReadFromStream and inB are derived from long counters (bytesReadFromStream is a long incremented by stream reads; inB is from getBytesInflated(), which reconciles Inflater byte counts across 2^32 wraps). The comment asserts the value 'is at most a single read() operation and can't exceed the range of int', but this relies on the invariant that the difference never exceeds one buffer (BUFFER_SIZE). If, for a malformed or large ZIP64 entry, bytesReadFromStream exceeds inB by more than Integer.MAX_VALUE, the narrowing cast could produce an unexpected/negative diff, which then feeds pushback(buf.array(), buf.limit() - diff, diff) and additional draining logic. A negative or wrong diff would lead to an incorrect pushback length/offset (buf.limit()-diff larger than the buffer or a negative length) and could throw or corrupt stream positioning. This is a robustness/parsing-integrity candidate dependent on the size accounting invariants holding.
missing_evidence: No empirical input was constructed to show bytesReadFromStream - inB can exceed Integer.MAX_VALUE.
The exact definitions and update sites of bytesReadFromStream and buf.limit() semantics in this class were not exhaustively read.
Whether other guards (e.g., limits on per-entry size) prevent the difference from growing this large was not confirmed.
preconditions: Processing an untrusted/crafted ZIP archive that can drive bytesReadFromStream and Inflater byte accounting apart by a large amount.
The documented invariant (difference <= one buffer) is violated by the crafted input or an accounting bug.
Reaching closeEntry() with an entry in the DEFLATED branch where inB uses getBytesInflated().
candidates.title: ZipArchiveInputStream.closeEntry() casts a long byte-count difference to int for pushback

counter_evidence: The guard appends File.separatorChar to targetDirPath before the startsWith comparison, which is the canonical fix for the prefix-sibling edge case, and changes.xml records this fix (release 1.18).
f.getCanonicalPath() is used (not absolute path), which resolves '..' segments.
A public test suite exists (ParameterizedExpanderTest) exercising expander behavior.
candidates.description: The high-level Expander.expand(...) builds the output file with 'new File(targetDirectory, nextEntry.getName())' and then validates 'f.getCanonicalPath().startsWith(targetDirPath)' where targetDirPath is targetDirectory.getCanonicalPath() with a trailing separator appended. This is the standard anti-traversal guard. The changes.xml notes a previously fixed path-traversal edge case (target directory name a prefix of a sibling directory). Because entry names come from the archive and can contain '..'/absolute components, correctness depends on: (a) the trailing-separator normalization always happening (it does), (b) canonicalization resolving symlinks deterministically, and (c) no platform-specific File.separator/case-insensitivity quirks. If canonicalization does not fully resolve an entry, or if the separator handling differs on the target platform, the startsWith check could be bypassed. This is presented as a residual-risk candidate, not a demonstrated bypass.
missing_evidence: No crafted archive entry name was run to demonstrate a bypass.
Behavior on Windows/UNC or case-insensitive filesystems was not analyzed.
Whether symlink entries inside the archive could still redirect writes was not traced through the SevenZFile/ZipFile writers.
preconditions: Caller uses Expander to extract an untrusted archive.
Crafted entry name attempts to escape targetDirectory.
Platform canonicalization/separator behavior interacts with the startsWith logic in an unexpected way.
candidates.title: Expander relies on canonical-path prefix check for archive entry names (potential path traversal if prefix/edges not covered)
